obligations.text: Gateway timeouts retry at most once, never twice.
Incoming webhooks verify HMAC-SHA256 signatures with timing-safe comparison.
Raw card numbers and CVVs are always redacted before logging.
HTTP requests exceeding 65,536 bytes are destroyed.
Health check route `/healthz` returns HTTP 200 with ok status.
Idempotency keys are held in memory with 24-hour TTL.
Working rules from CLAUDE.md require minimal diffs and running `node --test`.

planted_conflicts.description: README claims up to 3 retries and 48h idempotency TTL, while code performs 1 retry and uses 24h TTL.
ADR-0001 mandates HTTP 400 when Idempotency-Key is omitted, while test/webhook.test.js asserts HTTP 202.
docs/architecture.md describes active async reconciliation, while ENABLE_ASYNC_RECONCILE is hardcoded false in src/config/flags.js.
docs/roadmap.md plans ISSUE-14 multi-currency settlement, with no implementation in src/.

interview_answers.question: What is LedgerGate for and who uses it?
interview_answers.answer: Merchant checkout teams who need reliable payment webhook delivery without duplicate charges.

interview_answers.question: What must LedgerGate never do?
interview_answers.answer: Never charge a card twice after a timeout and never log raw card numbers or CVV values.

interview_answers.question: Which outcomes matter most?
interview_answers.answer: Zero duplicate charges per 10,000 requests and sub-3-second gateway timeout recovery.
